claim_text: ZmNRL1 has already been experimentally implicated in maize nitrogen-stress responses. We integrated sequence-validated B73 reference mapping, public transcriptomes and regulatory predictions with a separately defined maize–Sorghum comparative panel. The focal B73 raw-count nitrogen contrast in GSE252822 remained small (log2 fold change 0.042; adjusted P = 0.945), whereas GSE312408 TPM profiles were descriptive because of their measurement scale and metadata limitations. No motif family reached the within-species false-discovery threshold against matched upstream controls. Maize primary GO enrichment remained unexecuted because 5,345/187,842 annotation associations (2.8455%) failed ontology reconciliation; six local TargetFinder sites were predictions only. Genome-wide maize–Sorghum collinearity identified 670 blocks and 26 family-family anchor pairs. A 40-protein panel (23 maize, 17 Sorghum) was evaluated using dual-domain and full-length trees and four prespecified profile-mixture, occupancy-masked and Dayhoff-6 sensitivities. All taxa were retained despite four dual-domain and 18 full-length composition-test failures. Across 23 maize gene-level outcomes, ten computational candidates were robust, one retained a model caveat, eight supported possible co-orthology and four had contradicted exact-pair hypotheses. The focal ZmNRG2_001–Sb_GeneID_8069100 split had 100/100 SH-aLRT/UFBoot support in all six trees, despite focal full-length composition and missingness warnings; this does not establish functional equivalence. Separately, seven of eight validated intra-maize collinear pairs yielded exploratory Ka/Ks estimates (0.0776–0.3871); the ZmNRG2_011/013 estimate was withheld for alignment uncertainty, and no pair contained focal ZmNRL1. Saturation was not excluded and no divergence times were inferred. These findings prioritize bounded comparative hypotheses while preserving negative results, missing-data limitations and the distinction between computational support and demonstrated function.

claim_text:
Nitrogen is central to plant metabolism, yet its acquisition and efficient use remain major constraints in maize production (Congreves et al. 2021; Li et al. 2025). Nitrate also acts as a signal, and transport and signalling components coordinate responses to changing nitrogen availability (Cao et al. 2024). Evolutionary comparisons can prioritize experimentally testable candidates only when sequence homology is kept distinct from demonstrated physiological function.
In Arabidopsis thaliana, NITRATE REGULATORY GENE 2 (NRG2; AT3G60320) participates in nitrate signalling and has been reported to interact with NLP7 (Xu et al. 2016). NRG2-like proteins contain DUF630 and DUF632. Published work has described nitrate-responsive Arabidopsis and maize family members, including a maize member that complemented an Arabidopsis nrg2 phenotype (Li et al. 2024). ZmNRL1 has also been experimentally associated with the response to nitrogen limitation and plasma-membrane localization in maize (Zheng et al. 2025). Those observations are literature context, not experiments performed here.
A prior family survey reported 23 maize NRG2-like genes (Li et al. 2024). The present work does not claim first family discovery or a new functional characterization. It tests focal-gene identity and sequence provenance, evaluates comparative relationships in separately defined maize–Arabidopsis and maize–Sorghum panels, and examines model and alignment sensitivity without forcing a root or assigning function from a sister-tip relationship.
The objectives were to retain the validated B73 v4-to-v5 ZmNRL1 mapping; reanalyse focal expression under raw-count or descriptive TPM rules; test strand-correct upstream proxies against matched controls; reconcile organism-specific GO and local miRNA predictions; and evaluate independently supported collinearity and phylogenetic relationships. The maize–Sorghum extension specifically assessed composition, occupancy and model sensitivity for all 40 proteins and all 23 maize outcomes. Evidence-qualified intra-maize collinear pairs were screened separately for exploratory codon substitution estimates. No new wet-laboratory experiment was performed, and the unrun psRNATarget server analysis was not conflated with completed local TargetFinder predictions.
Public transcriptomes can test whether focal-gene abundance patterns are reproducible across experimental settings, but only after genome identifiers, matrix scale, tissue, treatment, time and replication have been reconciled. We therefore treated the two GEO studies as independent analyses rather than as exchangeable samples and retained published functional observations as external context.
We additionally characterized sequence-derived physicochemical properties for the frozen 38-protein panel to place the focal protein in a descriptive family context. This analysis was prespecified as exploratory and was not treated as experimental biochemical validation, a replicated lineage comparison, or evidence of nitrogen-responsive function.

claim_text:
The retained dataset comprised the entire retained sequences of 38 NRG2-like representatives, including the two partial Arabidopsis models with ordered DUF630–DUF632 architecture: 23 Zea mays proteins from B73 RefGen_v5 (Zm-B73-REFERENCE-NAM-5.0) and 15 Arabidopsis thaliana proteins from NCBI RefSeq TAIR10.1 (GCF_000001735.4_TAIR10.1). The frozen Stage 06 FASTA was checked residue-for-residue against the Stage 07 full-length FASTA, species representative FASTAs and original provider proteomes. Alias, gene, transcript, protein and FASTA identifiers were required to be one-to-one. The source FASTA was not modified; a derived FASTA changed headers only. ZmNRG2_001 maps to Zm00001eb303290, Zm00001eb303290_T001 and Zm00001eb303290_P001; AtNRG2_001 maps to AT3G60320, NM_115896.3 and NP_191591.2. Exact paths, SHA256 values and the reversible alias crosswalk are supplied in Tables S36–S37 and the claim-to-source matrix.
Full-length amino-acid sequences were analyzed with Biopython 1.87 Bio.SeqUtils.ProtParam.ProteinAnalysis under Python 3.11.15. Eleven prespecified sequence-derived descriptors were recorded: protein length, molecular weight, theoretical isoelectric point (pI), instability index, aliphatic index, grand average of hydropathy (GRAVY), aromaticity, predicted charge at pH 7, acidic-residue fraction, basic-residue fraction and hydrophobic-residue fraction. Acidic, basic and hydrophobic residue sets were D+E, K+R+H and A+V+I+L+M+F+W+Y, respectively. The aliphatic index was calculated as 100 × A fraction + 290 × V fraction + 390 × (I fraction + L fraction). Reduced and oxidized molar extinction coefficients were also recorded. A terminal stop, if present, was removed for calculation only while preserving the source sequence; noncanonical residues were to be recorded by exact position and any affected profile labelled approximate. No sequence required either treatment (38 exact-canonical; 0 approximate). The instability-index threshold of 40 was used only to assign an empirical sequence-based predicted class, not to infer measured stability.
Species-panel medians and interquartile ranges summarize the observed proteins. Prespecified two-sided Mann–Whitney comparisons were performed at the protein level for all 11 descriptors, followed by Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment across the 11 tests; Cliff's delta described the observed shift. The 38 proteins are phylogenetically related representatives from only two species, so proteins are not independent species or lineage replicates. These tests cannot establish lineage evolution, adaptation, nitrogen response or function. Focal context used robust z-scores and finite-sample empirical percentiles after excluding each focal protein from the matched background. A descriptive extreme required both |robust z| ≥3.5 and a ≤5th or ≥95th percentile. Same-species and full-family backgrounds overlap and are not independent validations.

location: 2.13. Post-synteny pair eligibility, codon substitution estimates and chromosome mapping
claim_text:
Eight unique intra-maize family-family MCScanX anchors from the validated M07B analysis defined the post-synteny pair set. The 13 endpoint representatives were matched through the M09C identity map to same-isoform official B73 NAM 5.0 CDS records, followed by exact translation, frame and stop-codon checks. Protein pairs were aligned sequentially using MAFFT v7.526 (--localpair --maxiterate 1000 --thread 2; Katoh and Standley 2013). PAL2NAL v14.1 (-output paml -nogap -codontable 1; Suyama et al. 2006) generated codon alignments, which were independently reconstructed from gap-free protein columns. Prespecified technical triage required at least 300 paired codons, 70% retention of the shorter protein and 30% paired-residue identity; passing these checks still required explicit alignment inspection. Eligible pairs were analysed with Yang–Nielsen estimation in PAML yn00 v4.10.10 using icode=0, weighting=1 and commonf3x4=0 (Yang and Nielsen 2000; Yang 2007). Nonfinite, negative or sentinel rates were unavailable, and zero Ks would produce NA Ka/Ks. Ks ≥2 was an identifiability warning rather than a universal saturation test; smaller Ks did not establish absence of saturation. Rates and standard errors were retained without formal selection or molecular-clock inference. The original species-specific chromosome maps remained coordinate evidence only.
For chromosome mapping, the frozen 23-gene B73 RefGen_v5 Stage08 table was reconciled against a current extraction from the same GFF3 and matched genome FASTA lengths. Fifteen Arabidopsis genes were separately extracted from matched TAIR10.1 RefSeq GFF3 and genomic FASTA resources. Start, end, inclusive midpoint, strand, placement class, assembly release and source checksums were retained. Maize and Arabidopsis chromosome lengths were plotted on independent species-specific axes.

claim_text:
The frozen 23-maize/15-Arabidopsis alias table was joined reversibly to the retained gene, transcript and protein identifiers and to release-matched annotations and genomic FASTA files (B73 RefGen_v5, Zm00001eb.1; and RefSeq TAIR10.1, GCF_000001735.4). The 5-prime boundary of each selected annotated transcript was used as a coordinate proxy; no experimentally mapped transcription start site was assumed. Up to 2,000 bp immediately upstream were extracted with 1-based closed coordinates: [transcript start - 2,000, transcript start - 1] on the positive strand and [transcript end + 1, transcript end + 2,000] on the negative strand, followed by reverse complementation for the latter. Requested and actual lengths, chromosome-boundary truncation, non-ACGT bases, target-gene-feature overlap, overlap with other annotated genes, strand, coordinate release, raw-forward and transcription-oriented SHA256 values were retained. Promoter-like sequence is therefore reported as an annotated selected-transcript 5-prime-boundary upstream proxy, not as an experimentally verified promoter or TSS.
JASPAR 2026 CORE non-redundant plant position-frequency matrices (CC BY 4.0; Ovek Baydar et al. 2026) were downloaded from the official JASPAR distribution and reconciled to its metadata. To avoid mixing organism availability, separate species-sourced libraries were constructed from records assigned to Zea mays (NCBI Taxonomy 4577; 91 motifs) and Arabidopsis thaliana (3702; 598 motifs). A separate zero-order nucleotide background was estimated from each species' 2-kb sequence set. FIMO 5.5.9 (Grant et al. 2011) scanned both strands using motif pseudocount 0.1, the species-specific background, a prespecified raw threshold of P < 1 x 10^-4 and a maximum of 1,000,000 stored scores. Sites with FIMO q <= 0.05 were retained for curation. Overlapping retained sites were clustered only within the same promoter and JASPAR TF-family category; the representative was selected by lowest q-value, then lowest P-value, then highest score. Motifs shorter than 6 bp, sites with sequence entropy <1.2 bits or maximum base fraction >=0.70, and sites within 25 bp of a proxy-sequence boundary were flagged rather than removed. Counts, presence/absence and density per kb include bona fide zeros; NA was reserved for an ineligible or unscannable sequence. These site scans were followed by the separate matched genomic-background analysis in Section 2.15. No direct maize-versus-Arabidopsis statistical comparison was performed. All sites are sequence-based predictions and do not demonstrate TF binding, nitrate responsiveness or transcriptional regulation.

location: 2.15. Matched genomic backgrounds and motif-family enrichment
claim_text:
The biological unit was one selected-transcript-boundary 2,000-bp upstream proxy per gene. Species were analysed separately. The primary foreground comprised 17 coordinate-PASS maize proxies and five coordinate-PASS Arabidopsis proxies; all-coordinate analyses retained the six maize and 10 Arabidopsis REVIEW cases as labelled sensitivities. From B73 RefGen_v5 and TAIR10.1 protein-coding annotations, strand-aware 2-kb upstream candidates were excluded for boundary clipping, ambiguous sequence, target membership or overlap, exact-sequence duplication, or incompatible overlap/partial-model context. A deterministic scarcity-first algorithm selected 10 globally unique controls per foreground block (minimum five), requiring absolute GC-fraction difference <=0.03 and ranking oriented 16-dinucleotide distance before local gene-density and chromosome-position differences. Same chromosome and strand were prioritised; seed 20261028 resolved exact rank ties.
Foreground and union-control sequences were scanned jointly within species by FIMO 5.5.9 using the frozen JASPAR 2026 species-matched CORE libraries (91 maize and 598 Arabidopsis motifs), a species-specific zero-order background, both strands, motif pseudocount 0.1, P < 1 x 10^-4 and a 10,000,000-score capacity. Q values were recomputed over each complete Stage 13 species universe. Sites with q <=0.05 were overlap-collapsed only within sequence and preregistered motif family. Motif width <6 bp, matched-sequence entropy <1.2 bits or maximum-base fraction >=0.70, and proximity within 25 bp of a proxy boundary were retained as explicit flags. AME was run with explicit controls only as an unpaired cross-check and did not supply the primary inference (McLeay and Bailey 2010).
For every prespecified family, the primary statistic was the mean across matched blocks of foreground presence minus mean control presence. One sequence in each foreground-plus-control block was relabelled as foreground in each of 100,000 Monte Carlo permutations; finite P values used (extreme + 1)/(B + 1). Ninety-five-percent intervals used 10,000 block bootstraps. One-sided enrichment P values were adjusted by Benjamini-Hochberg across all 23 maize or 55 Arabidopsis families. Prespecified sensitivities used all-coordinate blocks, seeds 20261029 and 20261030, low-complexity exclusion, nonoverlapping-cluster counts and JASPAR-class aggregation. Species were never pooled.

For an analysis passing its source gate, direct annotations were propagated through is_a and part_of relations. Right-tailed hypergeometric over-representation used a minimum background term size of five, retained every eligible BP, MF and CC term including k = 0, and applied one global Benjamini-Hochberg correction at FDR 0.05. The maize primary universe was exactly 44,303 unique source-listed genes and the study set exactly 23 genes, including unannotated members. location: 2.19. Local TargetFinder v1.7 candidate-site search and source-locked reconciliation

Species-separated eligible mature-miRNA sequences (325 maize; 586 Arabidopsis) were searched against 23 and 15 selected spliced transcripts, respectively, with cutoff score <=4. TargetFinder uses local Smith-Waterman complementarity followed by positional duplex scoring; its ssearch35_t requirement was satisfied by a separately tested, short-path ssearch36 compatibility setup and a genuine positive-control hit. All 911 individual query checkpoints passed the V16 execution audit and the V17 raw/sequence audit. Shannon single-base entropy <1.5 bits or homopolymers >=6 nt triggered exploratory low-complexity flags without post hoc deletion. This restricted-panel screen cannot be interpreted as genome-wide, experimental or psRNATarget V2 evidence. Score values are complementarity penalties, not calibrated binding probabilities (Fahlgren and Carrington 2010; Carrington Lab TargetFinder software).

location: 3.21. Exploratory substitution estimates after collinearity validation
claim_text: The eight validated intra-maize collinear pairs superseded the earlier topology-only eligibility screen. All 13 endpoint CDS translations matched their representative proteins exactly. Seven pairs passed alignment review and yielded exploratory estimates from 674–902 retained codons: Ka = 0.0238–0.2575, Ks = 0.1289–1.2656 and Ka/Ks = 0.0776–0.3871 (Table 15; Fig. 27; Supplementary Table S32). No zero Ks or prespecified Ks ≥2 warning occurred, but saturation was not independently excluded, especially for the two Ks estimates above one. ZmNRG2_011/013 retained 533 paired codons after gap removal, yet its divergent, indel-rich C-terminal correspondence was insufficiently credible; all substitution estimates were therefore withheld rather than obtained by arbitrary local trimming. No eligible pair contained focal ZmNRL1. The ratios below one are descriptive and not formal evidence of selection, functional conservation or duplication timing. Supplementary Fig. S8 is retained solely as a historical pre-synteny gate, not as the current eligibility outcome.

claim_text:
Exact focal-sequence validation, profile-HMM architecture tests and topology comparisons provide a traceable context for ZmNRL1. Shared DUF630/DUF632 architecture is consistent with family membership, but does not make all 38 proteins functionally interchangeable. Published experiments in Arabidopsis, selected maize NRG2-like genes and ZmNRL1 establish the biological context (Xu et al. 2016; Li et al. 2024; Zheng et al. 2025); the present study contributes computational provenance and sensitivity analysis rather than a new functional characterization.
Removing each flagged set left the topology among retained taxa unchanged (RF = 0); effects of individual excluded taxa were not tested separately. Conversely, the small full-length disagreement cannot be interpreted independently of extensive full-length alignment missingness and composition failures. The persistent nearest-tip association of ZmNRG2_001 with ZmNRG2_007 can motivate targeted comparison, yet primary support below the joint rule argues against a confident orthology claim.
The B73 raw-count contrast provides no adjusted-significant focal response after 48 h, while the TPM-only time course shows dataset-specific root and leaf profiles. Neither outcome negates published phenotypic and localization evidence or independently establishes a ZmNRL1 mechanism. Genotype, tissue, timing, normalization and reference-version differences prevent a pooled cross-study effect estimate. Expression changes in engineered overexpression material are not evidence of a native wild-type response; the focal genotype-by-nitrogen interaction also requires its own adjusted test. Transcript results are therefore expression associations and descriptive profiles, not functional proof.
Independent collinearity adds evidence beyond chromosome proximity or sequence similarity. Maize intra-genome anchors provide duplication-associated context, whereas maize–Sorghum anchor components constrain comparative relationship hypotheses. Neither collinearity nor reciprocal rank alone proves one-to-one orthology. The new 40-protein tree panel strengthens the focal maize–Sorghum relationship but does not resolve the weak focal maize–maize split in the separate 38-protein maize–Arabidopsis analysis. Single-isoform BUSCO completeness likewise does not date duplication or establish NRG2-like locus history.
Scientific limitations remain explicit. The inherited 38-protein maize–Arabidopsis analysis retains six original REVIEW flags, the additional AtNRG2_003 composition concern, 21/38 full-length composition failures and 29/38 high-gap sequences. The separate 40-protein maize–Sorghum panel has four dual-domain and 18 full-length composition failures; its five domain-completeness concerns and 31 unique high-gap taxa are not erased by a stable split. GSE312408 processing metadata remain contradictory; maize primary GO enrichment is source-gated; psRNATarget V2 is unrun; and local TargetFinder sites have no experimental validation. Ka/Ks estimates remain exploratory with saturation unresolved. Missing author declarations, public evidence deposition and journal-specific review further preclude submission readiness.
Physicochemical profiles add reproducible sequence-level description but no independent mechanistic evidence. The comparative panels cannot support replicated lineage contrasts, and the focal protein was not a prespecified descriptive extreme. Sequence-derived properties alone do not establish a novel biological function or journal suitability.
Ordered DUF630–DUF632 architecture, exact CDS translations and matched chromosome placement support identity and comparative context while preserving coding-structure caveats. The new collinear-pair estimates are limited to seven maize homolog pairs outside focal ZmNRL1. Their uncertainty, alignment dependence and unresolved saturation prevent an inference of positive selection or a molecular-clock date. Withholding ZmNRG2_011/013 estimates preserves a biologically important missing-data limitation rather than converting computational execution into evidence of validity.
The cis-regulatory analyses add coordinate-reproducible hypotheses, not a regulatory mechanism. The 38 windows are annotated transcript-boundary upstream proxies, 16 retain genomic-context REVIEW, and motif libraries differ markedly between species. FIMO/JASPAR site scanning was followed by a separate matched-background analysis; it was not PlantCARE analysis. No experimental TF-binding test was performed. The distal focal ERF/DREB-family prediction therefore remains a context-dependent candidate site rather than demonstrated nitrate-responsive control.
Matched genomic controls materially constrain the cis-motif interpretation. The absence of FDR-significant family enrichment, the Stage 13 loss of the focal MA2613.1 call at q <=0.05 and its 6/10 matched-control prevalence do not refute published ZmNRL1 biology; they show that these sequence matches alone cannot establish focal TF binding, enhancer activity, nitrate signalling or nitrogen-responsive transcription. Power is limited, especially for the five Arabidopsis PASS blocks; the windows remain annotated selected-transcript-boundary upstream proxies rather than experimentally verified promoters or transcription-start sites. Unequal species motif libraries also prohibit a direct evolutionary comparison.
The ontology audit illustrates why absence of a reported result must be classified by cause. Maize primary enrichment has no null-hypothesis tests because source reconciliation failed the fixed gate; the separate annotated-only sensitivity cannot repair that estimand. Conversely, the Arabidopsis nucleus term is a real statistical result under its stated universe, but its ISM-dominated evidence composition and complete 15/15 study annotation demand restraint. It supports enrichment of an annotation label, not universal experimental localization or a shared nitrate-signalling function.
The frozen full-proteome OrthoFinder analysis and the subsequent maize–Sorghum family study answer different comparative questions. The focal protein was unassigned in the maize–Arabidopsis reconciliation, whereas its maize–Sorghum relationship was robust under the six tree analyses; neither classification transfers physiological function. The source-locked mature-miRNA sequences support a restricted exploratory TargetFinder network, not a psRNATarget V2 result or direct interaction. Source-release provenance and the ssearch compatibility implementation remain qualified; low-complexity flags further limit specificity. Degradome/PARE or focused 5-prime RACE, together with relevant expression evidence, would be needed before assigning a regulatory mechanism.
Across-site profile mixtures and occupancy sensitivities answer complementary questions. C20 accommodates across-site compositional heterogeneity but is not a nonstationary lineage model; Dayhoff-6 reduces information as well as composition contrasts. Concordant focal support is consequently stronger computational evidence than a single tree, not proof that all substitution assumptions are satisfied. The profile-weight warning, composition failures and limited two-species sampling justify retaining scientific REVIEW. Broader validated taxon sampling and an independently justified nonstationary analysis could test unresolved cases, but their absence is not repaired by deleting inconvenient sequences.
The distinction between exact-pair support and component-level conservation changes the biological interpretation. Strongly supported groups containing several maize paralogs and one or more Sorghum members can support possible co-orthology without specifying an exclusive one-to-one partner. Conversely, an alternative maize–maize split can contradict an exact maize–Sorghum hypothesis while remaining consistent with homologous, collinear family membership. Thus ZmNRG2_011/013 and the ZmNRG2_005/023 and ZmNRG2_006/016 contexts should not be collapsed into either universal orthology or gene absence. Functional assays would be required to transfer nitrate-related roles.

claim_text: Exact focal v4-to-v5 identity, domain architecture, design-aware transcriptome analyses, matched upstream controls and source-gated annotation provide a reproducible framework for ZmNRL1. Collinearity and composition-aware phylogenetic sensitivity strengthen selected maize–Sorghum computational relationships while preserving possible co-orthology and conflicting exact-pair hypotheses. Seven non-focal intra-maize collinear pairs yield exploratory substitution estimates; one pair remains withheld and no divergence times are inferred. No matched-background motif category reached the FDR threshold in the primary analysis or the prespecified coordinate, tie-seed, low-complexity, cluster-count and JASPAR-class sensitivities. This negative finding applies to the present computational design and does not establish the absence of cis-regulatory control in vivo. The unexecuted maize primary GO test and six unvalidated local TargetFinder sites likewise delimit rather than establish mechanism. This version is an author-review manuscript candidate, not a claim of journal acceptance, submission readiness or new functional characterization.
